result:
task: DAEO-siiz (W2-52): run the W2-52 acceptance suites against the earlier engineer's code at `bd9fdfec` and change the code inside the allowed paths until they pass.
status: DONE. No change was needed: the code at `bd9fdfec` passes all 65 cases with the stand-in, the plain run fails only where expected, and W1-36 and the builder tests pass.
work_completed: Checked role, ticket, worktree and branch; all as expected. Read the ticket, the WBS limits on scope, the README's "The interface the cases hold", all five test files and the support code, CAP-44.f/h/k, `project.py`, `command.py` and the earlier code. Built a stand-in outside the tree and ran all four suites in the foreground. I also read the code looking for any way a gate could pass when it should not, and found none. Missing or unreadable A6/A8 records are refused (STAGE_MISSING / RECORD_UNREADABLE). The auditor's record must be committed at HEAD, readable, for this stage, have a `verdict`, carry a `Role:` trailer of exactly `independent-auditor`, write nothing under `governance/adoption/`, and have an `auditor_session` that is named and differs from every session that ran a stage and from the session running now. It must also list each checked record with that record's sha256 as it stands at HEAD. Only `pass` gives `met`. If a check throws an exception, that check is `not met`. A10's canary check is met only if the canary hit and the index was recreated. The gate refuses if its own record path already exists. No gate ever gives `accepted`. The skill text matches CAP-44.f/h/k. No commit was made because nothing changed.
files_changed: none in this session. `bd9fdfec` (the earlier session) changed `src/gov/adopt/lite_gates.py` (+261/−0), `src/gov/adopt/stages.py` (+5/−2), `template/governance/kernel/skills/adopt/SKILL.md` (+8/−2) and `tests/unit/adopt/test_lite_gates.py` (+149/−0): 423 added, 4 removed in total.
evidence: The commit is `bd9fdfec` "W2-52 (DAEO-siiz): the lite A7 and A10 gates and their stage records", with trailers `Task: DAEO-siiz`, `Role: engineer`, `Implements: DEC-741`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git log --oneline -2` shows `bd9fdfec`, then `fc4a3361`; `git status --short` is empty. `PYTHONPATH=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-52/src python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` prints `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-52/src/gov/__init__.py`. Every plain-run failure is `w2_52_support.py:364: AssertionError: gov adopt --lite does not take --stage A7` (32) or `... --stage A10` (22).
tests: (1) W2-52 with the stand-in: **65 passed in 205.16 s**, no skip. (2) W2-52 plain: **54 failed, 11 passed** (85.6 s; a second run with `--tb=line` gave the same counts in 105.4 s). All 54 failures are the "invalid choice" stop (32 A7, 22 A10). The 11 passes are the 4 skill cases, the 2 unchanged-behaviour cases, the fixture check and the 4 CAP-44.h rule rows. (3) W1-36: **84 passed** (17.9 s). (4) `tests/unit/adopt`: **46 passed** (14.2 s). No suite needed splitting.
discoveries: (a) The cases start `gov` children with a PYTHONPATH that W1-41's `environment()` sets itself, and the parent's PYTHONPATH does not reach them. A `sitecustomize.py` on the parent's PYTHONPATH alone therefore never reaches the children, so the stand-in also has to pass itself on to them (see below). (b) The read-only `/tmp/gov-cbm-1000` folder that stopped the earlier session did not get in the way here: every fixture got past A3. (c) The stand-in hides the system `/usr/lib/python3.12/sitecustomize.py`, which only installs Ubuntu's apport crash reporter (`apport_python_hook`); nothing in the tests depends on it.
risks: (1) The `stages.py` change also adds `lite_gates` to an existing import line (`from gov.adopt import lite_gates, project`) besides the two table entries and the routing in `run()`. The entries cannot work without it, but it is one line outside "the entries" taken literally. (2) A gate refuses (GATE_RECORDED) when its own record already exists, so re-running A7 or A10 after a failing record needs that record removed first. The README leaves re-runs uncovered. (3) A10 rebuilds the derived state in place (`gov.rebuild.command.run` with the adopt arguments; the rebuild reads none of them). (4) An A8 record with `retired: []` passes the retirement check, because it has nothing to check.
lessons: To show "only the tuple changes", the stand-in has to reach the `gov` children, whose environment the support code builds from scratch. Patching `subprocess.Popen.__init__` to put the stand-in folder at the front of a child's PYTHONPATH (only when that PYTHONPATH starts with this worktree's `src`) does it without editing any test or support file.
proposed_decisions: P-A (for the lead to take to the owner). **Question:** widen DAEO-siiz's allowed paths by one tuple: add `"A7"` and `"A10"` to `STAGES` in `src/gov/adopt/command.py`, as `("A0","A1","A2","A3","A4","A5","A6","A7","A8","A10")`. **Why now:** without it, `gov adopt --lite --stage A7|A10` stops at argparse's invalid choice, and 54 of the 65 cases stay red. **Options:** (1) widen by that one tuple now; (2) give the line to another ticket that owns `command.py`; (3) re-baseline. **Impact:** with the stand-in, which changes only that tuple, all 65 cases pass, so nothing else needs to change. **Reversibility:** fully reversible, one line. **Cost:** one line, then a re-run of W2-52 (about 3.5 min) and W1-41. **Recommendation:** option 1, ideally also updating the module docstring's stage list `<A0|…|A8>` in the same file. **Confidence:** high.
unresolved: (1) The `command.py` tuple (P-A). (2) README package P-1 (how a verdict names a missing gate record) is held only through the skill, as the cases chose; it is still open for W2-28/W2-30. (3) Re-running a gate is not designed.
recommended_next_action: Take P-A to the owner, add the one tuple, then re-run W2-52 plain (expect 65 passed) and W1-41.

**The stand-in and how it was placed.** It is `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-usain-gov-os-worktrees-W2-52/58d9b072-db73-4b64-b22f-62290081edfb/scratchpad/standin/sitecustomize.py`: outside the tree, not under `.gov-runtime/`, and gone when the session ends. It does two things:
- If `gov.adopt.command` imports from this worktree's `src/`, it sets `_command.STAGES = ("A0","A1","A2","A3","A4","A5","A6","A7","A8","A10")`. It changes nothing else in `gov`.
- It wraps `subprocess.Popen.__init__`: when a child's `env["PYTHONPATH"]` starts with `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-52/src`, it puts the stand-in folder in front, so the `gov` children load the same tuple. It changes nothing else in the child's environment.

The suite ran with `PATH=/home/usain/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH PYTHONPATH=<standin>:/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-52/src python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W2-52 -q -p no:cacheprovider -rs`. Before the suite I checked it: the parent printed this worktree's `gov/__init__.py` and the 10-stage tuple, and a child started with `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src` also printed the 10-stage tuple.

**The A7 and A10 records' form.** A gate commits one file in the adoption run's own folder, next to the A0 record:
- A7: `governance/adoption/A7-independent-migration-verification.md`
- A10: `governance/adoption/A10-independent-memory-verification.md`

Its frontmatter has `id: ADOPT-A7` / `ADOPT-A10`, `type: evidence`, `status: RECORDED`, `state_class: EVIDENCE`, `stage`, `session`, `stands_on` (sha256 of the A6 or A8 record), `result: pass|fail`, `commit` (HEAD it checked), and `records` (each checked record: stage, path, sha256). It also has `auditor` (record, sha256, commit, session, verdict) and `checks` (each check, `met`/`not met`, detail). A10 adds `retired`, `rebuild` (`digest`, `stores`) and `canaries` (lexical, semantic). It ends with `conditions` in W2-02's form (`name`, `source`, `state`; never `accepted`) and `wave_3`:
- A7 gives one condition, "lite A7 gate: … condition 4 …", with source `CAP-44.f`.
- A10 gives two: "lite A10 gate: … condition 6 …" (`CAP-44.f`) and "… derived state rebuilt from git (condition 9) …" (`CAP-44.h`).
- `wave_3` names CAP-44.k and CAP-47.a, and for A10 also A9 and CAP-49.

On a pass the answer is `ok: true` with `stage`, `record`, `conditions`, and for A10 the `digest`. On a failing check or a verdict other than `pass`, the record is committed and the gate then answers ADOPT_GATE_NOT_PASSED (`ok: false`). When the auditor's record is not a valid pass, or the record the gate stands on is missing, the gate refuses and writes nothing.
